article.contentMarkdown:
# Raksha Bandhan 2026: Date, Muhurat and the 27th-vs-28th Mix-Up

Raksha Bandhan 2026 falls on **Friday, 28 August 2026**, and the rakhi-tying window closes at **9:48 AM IST** — the instant Shravan Purnima ends. It opens at your local sunrise, which is why Kolkata gets 4 hours 27 minutes of it and Mumbai gets 3 hours 22.

We build the shareable pages people send on mornings like this: **2,973 personalised pages across 15 page types, made by 2,466 registered creators** since 12 March 2026. Which is why this guide leads with clock times: the two questions we get asked on a festival morning are *what time* and *will it arrive*.

The confusion over 27 versus 28 August is not a rumour. Purnima genuinely begins on the 27th. Bhadra genuinely covers most of that day. Below: the tithi, the Bhadra verdict, the muhurat for six cities, which nine states get the day off, and the one astronomical detail that makes 2026 unusual.

## Is Raksha Bandhan on 27 or 28 August 2026?

The 28th. Both dates appear in calendars because Shravan Purnima straddles them: it **begins at 9:08 AM on 27 August and ends at 9:48 AM on 28 August** in Delhi, per [Livemint's 25 August 2026 timing report](https://www.livemint.com/news/trends/raksha-bandhan-2026-date-august-27-or-28-know-the-right-day-check-shubh-muhurat-purnima-tithi-and-bhadra-kaal-11787630790054.html). Prokerala's panchang puts the start at 09:09 AM — a one-minute convention difference, not a disagreement.

The tie-break is the *udaya tithi* rule: the festival takes the day on which the relevant tithi is present at sunrise. On 27 August, Purnima arrives more than three hours after sunrise. On 28 August it is already running when the sun comes up, and it holds until 9:48 AM. So the 28th wins.

The Government of India agrees, which is the cleanest confirmation there is. The [2026 list of restricted holidays circulated under DoPT's OM No. 12/2/2023-JCA](https://dfe.gov.in/uploads/documents/list-of-restricted-holiidays-2026.pdf) carries "Raksha Bandhan — August 28 — Friday" as item 22 of 35. A gazette does not hedge.

## Does Bhadra kaal touch the 2026 morning muhurat?

No. This is the year's genuinely good news, and it deserves a plain sentence rather than the usual "avoid Bhadra" boilerplate. **Bhadra falls on 27 August and ends before sunrise on 28 August**, so it does not overlap the rakhi-tying period at all — Livemint states this directly, and the [Times of India's 22 August explainer](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/religion/festivals/raksha-bandhan-2026-is-raksha-bandhan-on-august-27-or-28-check-correct-date-bhadra-kaal-and-rakhi-muhurat/articleshow/133421773.cms) puts Bhadra on the 27th "till dusk".

That is the actual mechanism behind the date confusion, and almost nobody spells it out. Purnima starting on the 27th would ordinarily make it a candidate; Bhadra sitting on those hours removes it, leaving a clean window on the morning of the 28th.

Practically: on 28 August 2026 you need not time the ceremony around Bhadra at all. Every minute of the morning window is usable, which is unusual — in several recent years Bhadra ate the morning and pushed families into the afternoon.

## Rakhi muhurat 2026, city by city

Here is what the news coverage misses. **The closing time is national; the opening time is not.** 9:48 AM IST is the instant Purnima ends, and a tithi ends everywhere at once. The window opens at local sunrise, and India is 2,900 km wide.

Muhurat windows for 28 August 2026, from [Prokerala's location-aware panchang](https://www.prokerala.com/festivals/raksha-bandhan.php):

| City | Window opens (local sunrise) | Window closes (IST) | You get |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kolkata | 05:21 AM | 09:48 AM | 4 h 27 m |
| Delhi | 06:01 AM | 09:48 AM | 3 h 47 m |
| Chennai | 06:01 AM | 09:48 AM | 3 h 47 m |
| Bengaluru | 06:12 AM | 09:48 AM | 3 h 36 m |
| Mumbai | 06:26 AM | 09:48 AM | 3 h 22 m |

Kolkata gets 65 more minutes than Mumbai for the same festival. Ujjain, the classical reference meridian for Indian panchang, opens at 06:11 AM.

One honest wrinkle: Livemint and the Times of India both give Delhi as **5:57 AM to 9:48 AM**, a window of 3 hours 51 minutes, where Prokerala says 06:01 AM. Four minutes, from a different sunrise convention. Livemint also notes Gurgaon at 5:58 AM. If you are in a third city, look up your own sunrise rather than borrowing Delhi's — that is precisely how a panchang page computed for the wrong location ends up giving Indian readers a European muhurat.

## Where 28 August 2026 is an actual holiday

Raksha Bandhan is not a national holiday, and this catches people out every year. For central government offices it is a **restricted holiday** — item 22 of the 35 in that DoPT list — which means an employee must spend one of their limited optional days on it. The office itself stays open.

Nine states and union territories have declared it a public or regional holiday for 28 August 2026, according to [LatestLY's state-wise holiday breakdown](https://www.latestly.com/lifestyle/festivals-events/raksha-bandhan-2026-is-it-a-public-holiday-in-your-state-check-state-wise-status-for-august-28-festivities-7547082.html): Chhattisgarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, Gujarat, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh. Banks are shut in five of them — Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh.

The pattern is obvious: the holiday follows the festival's north-and-west heartland. If you are in Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata or Mumbai, 28 August 2026 is a normal working Friday, and the 9:48 AM deadline lands inside your commute.

## What makes 2026 different: an eclipse four minutes from the tithi's end

Purnima ends at the moment the moon is exactly full. Which means there is an independent way to check the panchang, and in 2026 it is unusually clean.

NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center [lunar eclipse canon for 2021–2030](https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/lunar.html) lists a **partial lunar eclipse on 28 August 2026**, greatest eclipse at 04:14:04 TD, Saros series 138, umbral magnitude 0.930, partial phase lasting 3 hours 18 minutes. Convert 04:14 UT to Indian time and you get **09:44 IST** — four minutes from the panchang's 09:48 AM tithi end. Two entirely separate computations, one Vedic and one astronomical, landing within four minutes of each other on the same instant.

Does it affect the ritual? No, and here is why: NASA lists visibility as the eastern Pacific, the Americas, Europe and Africa. **India is not on that list.** The moon is below the horizon in India at 09:44 IST, so there is no visible eclipse and, by the usual rule, no sutak to observe.

Two more 2026 specifics: 28 August is the second-latest Raksha Bandhan of the decade — 19 days after 2025's 9 August, beaten only by 30 August 2023 — and it falls on a Friday, a working day in most of the country.

## If you miss the 9:48 AM window

Plenty of families will. A 3-hour-22-minute window in Mumbai on a working Friday is tight, and the fallbacks are ranked, not equivalent.

### 1. Aparahna, roughly 1:38 PM to 4:11 PM in Delhi

The afternoon division, and the conventional second choice. Prokerala gives 01:38 PM to 04:11 PM for Delhi; Livemint puts it at roughly 1:46 PM to 4:20 PM. Note the tension nobody mentions: Purnima ended at 9:48 AM, so this window sits outside the tithi. Many households use it anyway, and many priests accept it.

### 2. Pradosh, roughly 6:43 PM to 8:59 PM in Delhi

The dusk division, and the third choice. Same caveat, further from the tithi. Prokerala's Delhi figures are 06:43 PM to 08:59 PM, with sunset at 06:43 PM.

### 3. A link timed to open at the muhurat

If the person is not in the room, the ceremony is a phone screen either way. A [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) or [the sister version](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-sister) takes a few minutes with a photo and a name, and can be built the night before to land inside the window. Across our platform, 51.1% of shared pages are opened on a phone and each one averages 12.2 views, so a link sent at 6 AM tends to be reopened through the day rather than seen once.

### 4. Nothing digital at all

If you are in the same house, put the phone down and tie the thread — a link is the wrong choice and we will say so. Our own numbers also say the rakhi templates are barely tested — **3 of those 2,973 pages** are Raksha Bandhan pages, with 39 recorded views between them. Too few to draw any conclusion from, and worth saying out loud. What we do have volume on is everything else:

| Page type | Pages created (of 2,973) | Share of all pages |
|---|---|---|
| "I love you" page (/love-gf) | 931 | 31.3% |
| Digital bouquet (/bouquet-gf) | 732 | 24.6% |
| Apology dashboard | 628 | 21.1% |
| Birthday page for a partner | 188 | 6.3% |

The reassuring number is completion: 99.4% of started pages get published and shared, 2,956 of 2,973. People who begin one finish it. You can [browse every SubhSandesh template](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) if the rakhi pages are not the right fit.

## Raksha Bandhan 2027 falls on Tuesday 17 August

Prokerala's 2020–2030 festival table gives **Tuesday, 17 August 2027** — 11 days earlier than 2026, because the lunar calendar drifts against the Gregorian one. A Tuesday is a working weekday in every state, holiday or not, so 2027 is the year to plan the ritual around office hours rather than assume a long weekend. Our sibling guides to Rakhi 2027 wishes and quotes cover the message itself.

One curiosity worth logging now: NASA's canon puts a **penumbral lunar eclipse on 17 August 2027** too, at 07:14:59 TD, Saros 148, visible only from the Pacific and the Americas. Two consecutive Raksha Bandhans on eclipse days is full-moon geometry, not an omen — but expect the question.

To re-date this page for 2027, only four values change: the date, the Purnima start and end, the per-city sunrise column, and the holiday notifications. Everything else — the udaya-tithi rule, the Bhadra mechanism, the national-close-local-open logic — holds every year.

## Sources

- Livemint, *Raksha Bandhan 2026 date: August 27 or 28?* — 25 August 2026. Purnima and Bhadra timings; Delhi and Gurgaon muhurat.
- The Times of India, *Is Raksha Bandhan on August 27 or 28?* — 22 August 2026. Bhadra on the 27th; Delhi window of 3 h 51 m.
- LatestLY, *Is it a public holiday in your state?* — 5 August 2026. State-wise and bank holiday status.
- Prokerala, Raksha Bandhan festival panchang — location-aware muhurat, Aparahna and Pradosha windows, 2020–2030 date table.
- Government of India, *List of Restricted Holidays 2026* (DoPT OM No. 12/2/2023-JCA) — Raksha Bandhan as item 22 of 35.
- NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, *Lunar Eclipses: 2021–2030* — the 2026 and 2027 eclipses. Undated reference publication.

Assigned lane F's named repositories were all unusable for a dated guide — theweek.in is at the domain cap and off-subject, pewresearch.org is full at 2/2, and sciencedaily.com, statista.com, lokniti.org and themarkup.org carry nothing on calendrical timing — so lane F was worked as media-and-data in substance, via Indian national newspapers. The nearest scholarly-grade source cited is NASA GSFC's lunar-eclipse canon, a reference publication rather than a peer-reviewed paper. auditReport.honestAssessment: This is a Gate 2 stretch and should be read as one. The SERP for `raksha bandhan 2026` is not a blog SERP: it is panchang engines, calendar stubs, two YouTube videos and rakhi ecommerce, and a blog post does not naturally occupy that page. Two things make it worth writing anyway — eternz.com, a small jewellery brand's blog, holds a page-one slot, so a content page can enter; and the DrikPanchang result that ranks was titled "…for Berlin, Berlin, Germany", a geo-mismatched computation holding a top slot on an India query. That weakness is what this post attacks: it is the only page found that prints the muhurat for six Indian cities and states the rule behind it — the 9:48 AM close is a tithi instant and therefore national, the open is local sunrise and therefore not — plus a nine-state holiday breakdown, the restricted-holiday status straight off the DoPT circular, and an independent cross-check of the tithi's end against NASA's eclipse canon that agrees to four minutes. None of the top results does any of that, and that is the honest reason an answer engine might cite this on the date-confusion and 'what time in my city' sub-questions. The realistic outcome is long-tail capture and answer-engine citation on those sub-questions, not position 1 on the head term: subhsandesh.in has no authority against a panchang engine on a calendrical query, and writing does not change that. It also cannot rank in time for 28 August 2026, three days out — the page is built to be re-dated, and the four values that change each year are named in the body.
